headline: Prisoner's base on the Pincio with Conie
summary: Roosevelt and his little sister Conie head up to the Pincio gardens in Rome and join a crowd of other children in a game of prisoner's base, then take their supper with their mother, Mittie. Back home, young Edith Carow writes Conie that she has been ordered to set her books aside.

events.detail: Plays prisoner's base with Conie and other children in the Pincio gardens
Edith Carow writes to Conie that her mother and nurse made her put away her books

letters.topic: Written to Conie: her mother and nurse Mame have taken away her books

uncertain: The Edith Carow letter was addressed to Conie, not TR; Mame is identified only as Edith's nurse.

headline: Jostled in the crowd at St. Peter's
summary: After hide-and-seek on the Pincio, the family goes to St. Peter's hoping to see the Pope. In the packed crowd a monk shoves young Theodore, and his father pushes the man back, hard.

events.detail: Joins a big crowd at St. Peter's hoping for a look at the Pope
A monk pushes the boy, and his father shoves the monk back with force

uncertain: The record says only 'the Pope'; Pius IX held the office in 1870.

headline: A birthday party for Ellie in Rome
summary: It is Ellie's birthday. Roosevelt plays horse on the Pincio, and at five o'clock a crowd of friends arrives for the party, where a girl named Elliese Van Schaack gives him a kiss.

events.detail: Party at 5 p.m. with many friends to mark Ellie's birthday
Gets a kiss from Elliese Van Schaack

uncertain: The record marks Ellie's birthday here and again on February 28, his 10th. Elliott Roosevelt was born February 28, 1860.

headline: Captain of the gendarmes
summary: A full day of games on the Pincio: fort, coins, horses, tag, and robbers-and-gendarmes, with Roosevelt leading the gendarmes as their captain.

events.detail: Plays fort, coins, horses, tag, and robbers and gendarmes, serving as captain of the gendarmes

headline: Bull, tag, and hide-and-seek
summary: Another afternoon on the Pincio, this time spent playing bull, tag, and hide-and-seek.

events.detail: Games of bull, tag, and hide-and-seek in the Pincio gardens

headline: Two brothers go to church alone
summary: Roosevelt and his younger brother Ellie attend church on their own. The diary also names two boys, Theodor Bronzen and Elliott de Briskey, apparently playmates.

events.detail: Goes to church alone with Ellie
The entry names Theodor Bronzen and Elliott de Briskey

uncertain: The entry names Elliott de Briskey and Theodor Bronzen without saying who they were, and the spellings may be off.

headline: A new ball for Conie
summary: On the Pincio, Roosevelt buys his sister Conie a ball.

headline: Rainy day of books and sisters
summary: Rain keeps the children indoors. Roosevelt reads about travel and geography and plays with his sisters Bamie and Conie.
uncertain: A word is unclear in the record and is left out.

headline: Ball and horse despite the weather
summary: The weather is poor, but Roosevelt still gets out to the Pincio for games of ball and horse.

events.detail: Plays ball and horse on the Pincio

headline: From the Pincio to the Vatican Loggia
summary: After time on the Pincio, Roosevelt visits the Vatican and its Loggia.

events.detail: Visits the Vatican and the Loggia

headline: Riding up top to Tivoli
summary: The family drives out by carriage to Tivoli, with Roosevelt perched on the driver's box in the bitter cold. They see the waterfalls and Hadrian's Villa.

events.detail: Carriage ride to Tivoli, sitting up on the box in the cold
Sees the falls at Tivoli and the Villa of Hadrian

headline: Ancient Rome while Ellie stays in bed
summary: With Ellie ill at home, the rest of the family rides by carriage through ancient Rome: the Forum, Trajan's Column, the Colosseum, and the Baths of Caracalla.

events.detail: Ellie is sick and stays behind
Carriage tour of the Forum, Trajan's Column, the Colosseum, and the Baths of Caracalla

headline: Church, Sunday school, and battles
summary: A Sunday of church and Sunday school, with battle games in between.

headline: Paintings at the Vatican
summary: Roosevelt goes to the Vatican to look at its paintings.

headline: Pincio and the Farnese pictures
summary: A morning on the Pincio, then paintings at the Farnese palace.

headline: Horse and Indian on the Pincio
summary: Roosevelt spends the day at the Pincio playing horse and Indian.

headline: A visit to Castel Sant'Angelo
summary: After the Pincio, Roosevelt sees the Castle of St. Angelo.

events.detail: Visits the Castle of St. Angelo

headline: Goodbyes in Rome as Father falls ill
summary: On a last day at the Pincio, Roosevelt plays horse and bids farewell to the friends he has made in Rome. His father is unwell, and guards go through the family's luggage.

events.detail: Says farewell to the children's friends in Rome

headline: Father gravely ill in Florence
summary: Now in Florence, Roosevelt plays in the garden while his father lies very sick.

headline: Father rallies; Mittie tells old stories
summary: His father is much improved. Roosevelt goes to church with Bamie and Ellie, plays coins and baby in the garden, and listens as his mother tells stories about her own girlhood.

events.detail: Goes to church with Bamie and Ellie
Plays coins, then baby in the garden
Mittie tells the children tales of her youth

headline: Muddy games and San Marco's paintings
summary: Roosevelt plays baby in the garden and ends up covered in mud, then visits the paintings at the convent of San Marco.

events.detail: Plays baby in the garden and gets thoroughly muddy
Sees paintings at the convent of San Marco

headline: A chilly trip up to Fiesole
summary: The family makes a cold outing to Fiesole, in the hills above Florence.

events.detail: Trip to Fiesole in cold weather

headline: Garden play and gallery paintings
summary: Roosevelt plays in the garden and looks at paintings in a Florence gallery.

headline: Soldiers, coins, and history
summary: In the garden Roosevelt plays soldiers and coins, and he spends time reading history.

events.detail: Plays soldiers and coins in the garden

headline: Feeling poorly, reading Greek history
summary: A bit under the weather, Roosevelt still plays soldiers and reads Greek history.

headline: Building miniature catacombs
summary: In the garden Roosevelt lays out tiny roads, palaces, and catacombs. He also visits the zoo, has tea, and reads.

events.detail: Builds small roads, palaces, and catacombs in the garden

headline: Headache keeps him from Sunday school
summary: Roosevelt is sick with a headache and misses Sunday school.

events.detail: Sick with a headache; skips Sunday school

headline: Ellie turns ten
summary: Roosevelt goes back to building little roads in the garden as his brother Ellie celebrates his tenth birthday.

headline: A visit to Mr. Elliott by the river
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie call on a Mr. Elliott, then play in a park along the river in Florence.
uncertain: A later note in the record suggests 'Mr. Elliott' may be spelled Eliot; who he was is not given. The river is presumably the Arno, which the record does not name.

headline: Watching the bears at feeding time
summary: With his father sick again, Roosevelt gets a haircut at the barber and visits the zoological garden, where he watches the bears being fed.

events.detail: Sees bears fed at the zoological garden

headline: The Uffizi and the Ponte Vecchio
summary: Roosevelt looks at pictures in the Uffizi, crosses the Ponte Vecchio, and plays in the garden.

headline: Three children, three little cities
summary: In the garden, Roosevelt, Ellie, and Conie each tend a miniature city of their own.

events.detail: Each child builds and plays with a small city in the garden

headline: Through 18 tunnels to Bologna
summary: The family travels to Bologna, passing through eighteen tunnels along the way, while Roosevelt reads Greek history.

events.detail: Train journey to Bologna through 18 tunnels

headline: Pigeons and carnival in Bologna
summary: Church is held at the hotel in Bologna. Roosevelt watches the pigeons and sees the carnival.

headline: Galleries, then a night train to Turin
summary: After visiting the art galleries in the rain, the family boards a train for Turin following dinner, and Roosevelt plays with his father.

events.detail: Visits the Bologna galleries in the rain
Takes the train to Turin after dinner

uncertain: The gallery's name is hard to read in the record; it is probably the Accademia di Belle Arti.

headline: Skeletons and armor in Turin
summary: In Turin, Roosevelt sees the armory, the royal palace, and animal skeletons at a museum.

events.detail: Visits the armory and the palace
Looks at animal skeletons in a museum

headline: Fourteen hours by rail into France
summary: A fourteen-hour train ride carries the family over steep mountains into France. This is the last entry in this volume of the boy's journal.

events.detail: Long train trip across steep mountains to France
Closes this volume of his journal

headline: Arriving in Paris, unwell
summary: After four more hours by train the family reaches Paris. Roosevelt is sick but still finds time for his coins.

headline: Playing at the Tuileries
summary: In Paris, Roosevelt plays in the Tuileries, visits the shoemakers, and plays coins.

headline: Toy boats and soldiers
summary: A day of play with boats and toy soldiers in Paris.

headline: Snowy Sunday in Paris
summary: Snow falls on a Sunday of church and Sunday school, with coins for play.

headline: A frozen fountain and the Lampsons
summary: Roosevelt sails his boats, finds the fountain frozen over, and spends time with the Lampson family's Johnny.

events.detail: Plays with boats; the fountain has frozen

uncertain: The record says only 'Johnny Lampsons', perhaps meaning a visit to the Lampson home.

headline: Ice on the fountain still
summary: The fountain is still iced over. Roosevelt plays soldiers and hide-and-seek.

headline: Shut in a dark closet
summary: On a rainy day Roosevelt plays soldiers and reads. The diary also mentions a dark closet.

events.detail: Plays soldiers indoors in the rain
A dark closet figures in the day's entry

uncertain: The record mentions a 'dark closet' without explaining it; compare the closet episode of March 28.

headline: A glimpse of the Emperor
summary: Johnny Lampson comes to dinner after a day of soldiers and boats, and Roosevelt catches sight of Emperor Napoleon III.

events.detail: Johnny Lampson dines with the family

uncertain: The record says only 'the emperor'; Napoleon III ruled France in 1870.

headline: Sailing boats with Ellie
summary: Roosevelt and Ellie spend the day sailing their toy boats.

headline: Choosing a school for Bamie
summary: Feeling a little sick, Roosevelt goes by train to Fontainebleau to see the palace. The family inspects Les Ruches, Mlle. Marie Souvestre's private school, where Bamie will remain when the rest go home to America.

events.detail: Train to Fontainebleau; visits the palace
Family looks over Les Ruches, the school run by Marie Souvestre, for Bamie

headline: Sunday church in Paris
summary: Roosevelt goes to church in Paris.

references.title: Cutright, Theodore Roosevelt: The Making of a Conservationist

uncertain: The record attaches a note here about Mr. Elliott, possibly Eliot (see March 1).

headline: Rain, soldiers, and boats
summary: A wet day passed with toy soldiers and boats.

headline: More rain, more soldiers
summary: Rain again, and more games with toy soldiers.

headline: A walk and the soldiers
summary: Roosevelt takes a walk and plays with his soldiers.

headline: Boat, ball, and soldiers
summary: Roosevelt plays with his boat, a ball, and his soldiers.

headline: Uncle Silas Weir Roosevelt dies
summary: While Roosevelt plays ball in a Paris garden, his uncle Silas Weir Roosevelt dies back in the United States.

events.detail: His uncle Silas Weir Roosevelt dies

headline: Garden and soldiers
summary: Time in the garden and with the toy soldiers.

headline: Church with Bamie
summary: Roosevelt and Bamie go to church together, followed by a walk, coins, and Sunday school.

events.detail: Goes to church with Bamie, then Sunday school

headline: Forty-five minutes locked in a closet
summary: Roosevelt spends three-quarters of an hour shut inside a closet, and plays soldiers.

events.detail: Spends 45 minutes shut inside a closet

uncertain: The record does not say how or why he came to be locked in.

headline: Window-shopping for soldiers
summary: Roosevelt plays boat and marbles and gazes at the toy soldiers in a shop.

events.detail: Looks at soldiers in a store

headline: Tag and stamps
summary: Outdoors in the garden for tag, then time with his stamps.

headline: A visit to the Louvre
summary: Roosevelt is taken to the Louvre.

headline: Tea with Fanny Lampson
summary: After the Tuileries garden, Fanny Lampson comes over to play and stays for tea.

events.detail: Fanny Lampson visits to play and for tea

headline: Tombs at Pere Lachaise
summary: Roosevelt tours the tombs of Pere Lachaise cemetery and the Pantheon.

events.detail: Sees the tombs at Pere Lachaise

headline: Sunday church
summary: Roosevelt attends church in Paris.

headline: Back to the Tuileries garden
summary: Another day of play in the Tuileries garden.

headline: Looking at the animals
summary: Roosevelt goes to see animals in Paris.
uncertain: The record does not say where the animals were seen.

headline: The porcelain works at Sevres
summary: The family drives by carriage to Sevres and tours the china factory.

events.detail: Carriage trip to Sevres to see the porcelain factory

headline: Sitting for photographs
summary: Roosevelt has his photograph taken and takes a French lesson.

headline: French class after the Tuileries
summary: A visit to the Tuileries, then French class.

headline: A helmet and a bow
summary: Roosevelt buys himself a helmet and a bow and arrows.

events.detail: Buys a helmet and a bow with arrows

headline: Church and a walk
summary: Sunday brings church and a walk.

headline: Emperor and Prince Imperial review troops
summary: Roosevelt watches Napoleon III and the young Prince Imperial review the French troops in Paris.

events.detail: Sees the Emperor and the Prince Imperial review soldiers
people: Napoleon Eugene Louis Bonaparte, Prince Imperial

people.name: Napoleon Eugene Louis Bonaparte, Prince Imperial

uncertain: The record names only 'the Emperor and Prince Imperial'; they are identified as Napoleon III and his son.

headline: Day trip to Versailles
summary: The family travels an hour and a half to Versailles.

events.detail: Trip of an hour and a half to Versailles

headline: Nine boys and an army indoors
summary: Nine boys fill the house for a game of soldiers.

events.detail: Indoor soldiers game with nine boys

headline: Soldiers, and a scrap
summary: During a day of soldiers, Roosevelt gets into a fight.

headline: Ten soldiers and a ball
summary: Roosevelt plays soldiers, with ten of them noted, and ball.
uncertain: The meaning of '10 soldiers' is unclear: toy soldiers or ten boys playing.

headline: A sick boy goes to Fontainebleau
summary: After a rough night, Roosevelt goes to Fontainebleau and plays in the garden, though he is ill.

headline: The best Easter of his life
summary: At Fontainebleau, Roosevelt walks in the woods and hunts Easter eggs, and calls it the happiest Easter he has known.
uncertain: Place inferred from the surrounding Fontainebleau entries; the day's line gives none.

headline: Parents and Bamie head to Paris
summary: His father, mother, and Bamie go up to Paris while Roosevelt stays at Fontainebleau playing in the garden.

events.detail: His parents and Bamie go to Paris

headline: By train back to Paris
summary: Roosevelt returns to Paris by train.

headline: Sick in Paris
summary: Roosevelt is ill.

headline: Reading in the shade
summary: Still sick, Roosevelt reads in the shade.

headline: French lesson and garden
summary: A French lesson and time in the garden.

headline: Climbing rocks at Fontainebleau
summary: Roosevelt takes the train to Fontainebleau and scrambles over the rocks.

headline: Rocks in the park
summary: A day in the park at Fontainebleau among the rocks.

events.detail: Explores the park and its rocks

headline: The Tuileries and the Champs-Elysees
summary: Back in Paris, Roosevelt visits the Tuileries and the Champs-Elysees.

events.detail: Visits the Tuileries and the Champs-Elysees

headline: A full day of lessons and play
summary: Garden, soldiers, a French lesson, reading, and play fill the day.

headline: Rain in Paris
summary: A rainy day in Paris.

headline: Tag and coins in the rain
summary: Despite rain, Roosevelt plays tag and coins and has a French lesson.

headline: Horse and fort
summary: Roosevelt plays horse and fort and reads.

headline: Tearful goodbye to Bamie; on to London
summary: The family leaves Bamie behind at school and everyone cries. After five hours on the train and a slightly queasy Channel crossing from Boulogne to Folkestone, they reach London. Years later Roosevelt said plainly that he disliked the whole trip.

events.detail: Bamie stays in France; the family weeps at parting
Five-hour train ride, then across the Channel from Boulogne to Folkestone
A little seasick on the crossing
Last entry in this volume of his journal

tr_quotes.text: I do not think I gained anything from this particular trip abroad. I cordially hated it, as did my younger brother and

uncertain: The quote is cut off mid-sentence in the record and seems to come from TR's later Autobiography, not his 1870 diary.

headline: Sent from the table in London
summary: There is no church today. Roosevelt goes to Hyde Park, and at a meal he dips his fingers into the butter dish and is dismissed from the table.

events.detail: Sent away from the table for sticking his hand in the butter

headline: A gift of stamps from a stranger
summary: Roosevelt goes to Wells and to a bank, where a kind gentleman hands him some stamps.

events.detail: Goes to Wells and a bank
A friendly gentleman gives him stamps

uncertain: 'Wells' is unclear in the record; it may be a person, a firm or a place.

headline: Windsor Castle and Eton
summary: A train ride to Windsor Castle, where Roosevelt sees the farm, stables, and castle, then a stop at Eton before heading home.

events.detail: Train to Windsor; sees the castle, farm, and stables

headline: A day at the London zoo
summary: Roosevelt visits the zoo in London.

headline: A walk in Hyde Park
summary: Roosevelt walks in Hyde Park.

headline: Stamps and the zoo again
summary: Roosevelt works on his stamps and returns to the zoo.

headline: Liverpool and Uncle Irvine
summary: Roosevelt travels to Liverpool, with his parents coming along after, and meets his uncle Irvine Bulloch. Coins round out the day.

events.detail: Goes to Liverpool; his parents follow

headline: Sunday in Liverpool
summary: Church and a walk in Liverpool.

headline: Cousins, the beach, and rare stamps
summary: Roosevelt sees his cousins, goes to the beach, and comes across some rare stamps.
uncertain: Cousins are not named; likely the Bulloch children.

headline: Digging trenches at Aunt Hattie's
summary: At Waterloo, near Liverpool, with Aunt Hattie, Roosevelt digs burrows and trenches.
uncertain: The record gives only 'Aunt Hattie'; she is likely Harriott Bulloch, wife of James Dunwoody Bulloch.

headline: Rainy reading day at Waterloo
summary: Rain at Waterloo, and Roosevelt reads.

headline: A cave in the sand hills
summary: Roosevelt plays in the sand hills and finds a cave, then rides into Liverpool in the afternoon.

events.detail: Plays in the sand hills; a cave

headline: Waxworks and farewells
summary: A visit to the waxworks, then goodbyes to the Liverpool cousins.

headline: Aboard the Russia, homeward bound
summary: The family sails on the screw steamer Russia across the Irish Sea. It rains, but Roosevelt does not get seasick.

headline: Nine hours at Queenstown
summary: With no church aboard, the ship lies at Queenstown, Ireland, for nine hours. Sunday school is held.

events.detail: Ship stops nine hours at Queenstown

headline: Seasick, then shipboard friends
summary: The first days at sea are rough and Roosevelt gets seasick, but he recovers fast, makes friends, and plays on deck.

Makes friends and plays on deck

headline: Crossing the Atlantic
summary: The Russia steams on across the Atlantic; the diary records only that the family is at sea.

headline: Sixteen children play Colosseum
summary: Church and Sunday school at sea, a fight in the morning, then tag, hide-and-seek, and a game of Colosseum with sixteen children.

events.detail: Tag, hide-and-seek, and Colosseum with 16 children

headline: Whales off the bow
summary: The ship takes on a pilot, and Roosevelt sees whales, one of which sprays him with water. His travel journal ends here.

headline: Hip! Hurrah! Home to America
summary: America comes into view. The Russia passes Sandy Hook into New York Bay, and friends meet the family at the pier.

events.detail: Sights America, passes Sandy Hook into New York Bay

headline: Breakfast and Jimmy's collection
summary: Back in New York, Roosevelt goes round to a neighbor's for breakfast, sees his friend Jimmy, and looks over a collection.

events.detail: Sees Jimmy and examines a collection

tr_quotes.text: We went round and had breakfast at her house

uncertain: The 'her' whose house they visited, and Jimmy's surname, are not given.

headline: Home all day with Jimmie and Dora
summary: Roosevelt spends the whole day at home playing with Jimmie and chatting with Dora.

events.detail: Plays at home with Jimmie and talks with Dora

tr_quotes.text: We stayed at our house the whole day playing with Jimmie and talked with Dora.

uncertain: Jimmie appears to be the Jimmy of May 26; Dora is not identified.

headline: The rest of the family goes to the country
summary: While the others head out to the country, Roosevelt stays in the city with his parents and has Jimmie over to play.

events.detail: Stays in New York with his father and mother

tr_quotes.text: the rest went in to the country

headline: Off to Philadelphia with Aunt Susy
summary: No church today. Roosevelt walks with Evelen and reads, then sets off with Aunt Susy on a four-hour train trip to Philadelphia, reading and writing along the way.

events.detail: Four-hour rail trip to Philadelphia with Aunt Susy, reading and writing

tr_quotes.text: I go with Aunt Susy to Philadelphia to day

uncertain: The record gives no surnames. Aunt Susy is probably Mittie's half-sister Susan West; Evelen is unidentified.

headline: China animals and strawberry ice cream
summary: In Philadelphia Roosevelt buys little china animals, shares strawberry ice cream with Aunt Susy, and sees the U.S. Mint. His father arrives that night and goes to the Union League Club.

events.detail: Buys china animals; strawberry ice cream with Aunt Susy
His father arrives and visits the Union League Club

tr_quotes.text: I bought some china animals and Aunt Susy and I had strawberry ice cream

uncertain: The record does not make clear whether TR went to the Union League Club or only his father did.

headline: The young naturalist starts collecting
summary: Roosevelt begins collecting every kind of wild creature he can find, launching a boyhood natural history collection.

events.detail: Starts gathering specimens of all kinds of wildlife
